   297→    def build_tokenized_answer(self, prompt, answer):
   298→        """
   299→        Llama tokenizer does satisfy `enc(a + b) = enc(a) + enc(b)`.
   300→        It does ensure `enc(a + b) = enc(a) + enc(a + b)[len(enc(a)):]`.
   301→        Reference:
   302→            https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness/pull/531#issuecomment-1595586257
   303→        """
   304→
   305→        full_tokenized = self.tokenizer(prompt + answer, add_special_tokens=False)
   306→        prompt_input_ids = self.tokenizer(prompt, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
   307→
   308→        answer_input_ids = full_tokenized["input_ids"][len(prompt_input_ids) :]
   309→        answer_attention_mask = full_tokenized["attention_mask"][len(prompt_input_ids) :]
   310→
   311→        # Concat tokens to form `enc(a) + enc(a + b)[len(enc(a)):]`
   312→        full_concat_input_ids = np.concatenate([prompt_input_ids, answer_input_ids])
   313→
   314→        # Prepare input tokens for token by token comparison
   315→        full_input_ids = np.array(full_tokenized["input_ids"])
   316→
   317→        if len(full_input_ids) != len(full_concat_input_ids):
   318→            raise ValueError("Prompt input ids and answer input ids should have the same length.")
   319→
   320→        # On some tokenizers, like Llama-2 tokenizer, there are occasions where tokens
   321→        # can be merged together when tokenizing prompt+answer. This could result
   322→        # on the last token from the prompt being different when tokenized on its own
   323→        # vs when done as prompt+answer.
   324→        response_token_ids_start_idx = len(prompt_input_ids)
   325→
   326→        # If tokenized prompt is different than both prompt+answer, then it means the
   327→        # last token has changed due to merging.
   328→        if prompt_input_ids != full_tokenized["input_ids"][:response_token_ids_start_idx]:
   329→            response_token_ids_start_idx -= 1
   330→
   331→        prompt_input_ids = full_tokenized["input_ids"][:response_token_ids_start_idx]
   332→        prompt_attention_mask = full_tokenized["attention_mask"][:response_token_ids_start_idx]
   333→
   334→        if len(prompt_input_ids) != len(prompt_attention_mask):
   335→            raise ValueError("Prompt input ids and attention mask should have the same length.")
   336→
   337→        answer_input_ids = full_tokenized["input_ids"][response_token_ids_start_idx:]
   338→        answer_attention_mask = full_tokenized["attention_mask"][response_token_ids_start_idx:]
   339→
   340→        return dict(
   341→            prompt_input_ids=prompt_input_ids,
   342→            prompt_attention_mask=prompt_attention_mask,
   343→            input_ids=answer_input_ids,
   344→            attention_mask=answer_attention_mask,
   345→        )

   349→
   350→        At this stage, we don't convert to PyTorch tensors yet; we just handle the truncation
   351→        in case the prompt + chosen or prompt + rejected responses is/are too long. First
   352→            we truncate the prompt; if we're still too long, we truncate the chosen/rejected.
   353→
   354→        We also create the labels for the chosen/rejected responses, which are of length equal to
   355→            the sum of the length of the prompt and the chosen/rejected response, with
   356→            label_pad_token_id  for the prompt tokens.
   357→        """
   358→        batch = {}
   359→        prompt = feature["prompt"]
   360→        chosen = feature["chosen"]
   361→        rejected = feature["rejected"]

   363→        if not self.is_encoder_decoder:

   365→            #  1. https://github.com/huggingface/trl/issues/907
   366→            #  2. https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness/pull/531#issuecomment-1595586257
   367→            #  3. https://github.com/LianjiaTech/BELLE/issues/337
   368→
   369→            if not isinstance(prompt, str):
   370→                raise ValueError(f"prompt should be an str but got {type(prompt)}")
   371→            prompt_tokens = self.tokenizer(prompt, add_special_tokens=False)
   372→            prompt_tokens = {f"prompt_{k}": v for k, v in prompt_tokens.items()}
   373→
   374→            if not isinstance(chosen, str):
   375→                raise ValueError(f"chosen should be an str but got {type(chosen)}")
   376→            chosen_tokens = self.build_tokenized_answer(prompt, chosen)
   377→
   378→            if not isinstance(rejected, str):
   379→                raise ValueError(f"rejected should be an str but got {type(rejected)}")
   380→            rejected_tokens = self.build_tokenized_answer(prompt, rejected)
   381→
   382→            # Last prompt token might get merged by tokenizer and
   383→            # it should not be included for generation if that happens
   384→            prompt_len_input_ids = len(prompt_tokens["prompt_input_ids"])
   385→
   386→            chosen_prompt_len_input_ids = len(chosen_tokens["prompt_input_ids"])
   387→            rejected_prompt_len_input_ids = len(rejected_tokens["prompt_input_ids"])
   388→            prompt_len_input_ids = min(chosen_prompt_len_input_ids, rejected_prompt_len_input_ids)
   389→
   390→            for k, v in prompt_tokens.items():
   391→                prompt_tokens[k] = v[:prompt_len_input_ids]
   392→
   393→            # Make sure prompts only have one different token at most an
   394→            # and length only differs by 1 at most
   395→            num_diff_tokens = sum(
   396→                [a != b for a, b in zip(chosen_tokens["prompt_input_ids"], rejected_tokens["prompt_input_ids"])]
   397→            )
   398→            num_diff_len = abs(chosen_prompt_len_input_ids - rejected_prompt_len_input_ids)
   399→            if num_diff_tokens > 1 or num_diff_len > 1:
   400→                raise ValueError(
   401→                    "Chosen and rejected prompt_input_ids might only differ on the "
   402→                    "last token due to tokenizer merge ops."
   403→                )
   404→
   405→            # add BOS token to head of prompt. Avoid adding if it's already there
   406→            bos_token_id = self.tokenizer.bos_token_id
   407→            if prompt_len_input_ids == 0 or bos_token_id != prompt_tokens["prompt_input_ids"][0]:
   408→                prompt_tokens["prompt_input_ids"] = [bos_token_id] + prompt_tokens["prompt_input_ids"]
   409→                prompt_tokens["prompt_attention_mask"] = [1] + prompt_tokens["prompt_attention_mask"]
   410→            if chosen_prompt_len_input_ids == 0 or bos_token_id != chosen_tokens["prompt_input_ids"][0]:
   411→                chosen_tokens["prompt_input_ids"] = [bos_token_id] + chosen_tokens["prompt_input_ids"]
   412→                chosen_tokens["prompt_attention_mask"] = [1] + chosen_tokens["prompt_attention_mask"]
   413→            if rejected_prompt_len_input_ids == 0 or bos_token_id != rejected_tokens["prompt_input_ids"][0]:
   414→                rejected_tokens["prompt_input_ids"] = [bos_token_id] + rejected_tokens["prompt_input_ids"]
   415→                rejected_tokens["prompt_attention_mask"] = [1] + rejected_tokens["prompt_attention_mask"]
   416→
   417→            # add EOS token to end of answer. Avoid adding if it's already there
   418→            eos_token_id = self.tokenizer.eos_token_id
   419→            if len(chosen_tokens["input_ids"]) == 0 or eos_token_id != chosen_tokens["input_ids"][-1]:
   420→                chosen_tokens["input_ids"].append(eos_token_id)
   421→                chosen_tokens["attention_mask"].append(1)
   422→            if len(rejected_tokens["input_ids"]) == 0 or eos_token_id != rejected_tokens["input_ids"][-1]:
   423→                rejected_tokens["input_ids"].append(eos_token_id)
   424→                rejected_tokens["attention_mask"].append(1)
   425→
   426→            longer_response_length = max(len(chosen_tokens["input_ids"]), len(rejected_tokens["input_ids"]))
   427→
   428→            # if combined sequence is too long, truncate the prompt
   429→            for answer_tokens in [chosen_tokens, rejected_tokens, prompt_tokens]:
   430→                if len(answer_tokens["prompt_input_ids"]) + longer_response_length > self.max_length:
   431→                    if self.truncation_mode == "keep_start":
   432→                        for k in ["prompt_input_ids", "prompt_attention_mask"]:
   433→                            answer_tokens[k] = answer_tokens[k][: self.max_prompt_length]
   434→                    elif self.truncation_mode == "keep_end":
   435→                        for k in ["prompt_input_ids", "prompt_attention_mask"]:
   436→                            answer_tokens[k] = answer_tokens[k][-self.max_prompt_length :]
   437→                    else:
   438→                        raise ValueError(f"Unknown truncation mode: {self.truncation_mode}")
   439→
   440→            # if that's still too long, truncate the response
   441→            for answer_tokens in [chosen_tokens, rejected_tokens]:
   442→                if len(answer_tokens["prompt_input_ids"]) + longer_response_length > self.max_length:
   443→                    for k in ["input_ids", "attention_mask"]:
   444→                        answer_tokens[k] = answer_tokens[k][: self.max_length - self.max_prompt_length]
   445→
   446→            # Create labels
   447→            chosen_sequence_tokens = {
   448→                k: chosen_tokens[f"prompt_{k}"] + chosen_tokens[k] for k in ["input_ids", "attention_mask"]
   449→            }
   450→            rejected_sequence_tokens = {
   451→                k: rejected_tokens[f"prompt_{k}"] + rejected_tokens[k] for k in ["input_ids", "attention_mask"]
   452→            }
   453→            chosen_sequence_tokens["labels"] = chosen_sequence_tokens["input_ids"][:]
   454→            chosen_sequence_tokens["labels"][: len(chosen_tokens["prompt_input_ids"])] = [
   455→                self.label_pad_token_id
   456→            ] * len(chosen_tokens["prompt_input_ids"])
   457→            rejected_sequence_tokens["labels"] = rejected_sequence_tokens["input_ids"][:]
   458→            rejected_sequence_tokens["labels"][: len(rejected_tokens["prompt_input_ids"])] = [
   459→                self.label_pad_token_id
   460→            ] * len(rejected_tokens["prompt_input_ids"])
   461→
   462→            for k, toks in {
   463→                "chosen_": chosen_sequence_tokens,
   464→                "rejected_": rejected_sequence_tokens,
   465→                "": prompt_tokens,
   466→            }.items():
   467→                for type_key, tokens in toks.items():
   468→                    if type_key == "token_type_ids":
   469→                        continue
   470→                    batch[f"{k}{type_key}"] = tokens
   471→
   472→        else:
   473→            chosen_tokens = self.tokenizer(
   474→                chosen, truncation=True, max_length=self.max_target_length, add_special_tokens=True
   475→            )
   476→            rejected_tokens = self.tokenizer(
   477→                rejected, truncation=True, max_length=self.max_target_length, add_special_tokens=True
   478→            )
   479→            prompt_tokens = self.tokenizer(
   480→                prompt, truncation=True, max_length=self.max_prompt_length, add_special_tokens=True
   481→            )
   482→
   483→            batch["chosen_labels"] = chosen_tokens["input_ids"]
   484→            batch["rejected_labels"] = rejected_tokens["input_ids"]
   485→            batch["prompt_input_ids"] = prompt_tokens["input_ids"]
   486→            batch["prompt_attention_mask"] = prompt_tokens["attention_mask"]
   487→
   488→            if model is not None and hasattr(model, "prepare_decoder_input_ids_from_labels"):
   489→                batch["rejected_decoder_input_ids"] = model.prepare_decoder_input_ids_from_labels(
   490→                    labels=torch.tensor(batch["rejected_labels"])
   491→                )
   492→                batch["chosen_decoder_input_ids"] = model.prepare_decoder_input_ids_from_labels(
   493→                    labels=torch.tensor(batch["chosen_labels"])
   494→                )
   495→
   496→        return batch

   498→    @staticmethod
   499→    def concatenated_inputs(
   500→        batch: Dict[str, Union[List, torch.LongTensor]],
   501→        is_encoder_decoder: bool = False,
   502→        label_pad_token_id: int = -100,
   503→        padding_value: int = 0,
   504→        device: Optional[torch.device] = None,
   505→    ) -> Dict[str, torch.LongTensor]:
   506→        """Concatenate the chosen and rejected inputs into a single tensor.
   507→
   508→        Args:
   509→            batch: A batch of data. Must contain the keys 'chosen_input_ids' and 'rejected_input_ids', which are tensors of shape (batch_size, sequence_length).
   510→            is_encoder_decoder: Whether the model is an encoder-decoder model.
   511→            label_pad_token_id: The label pad token id.
   512→            padding_value: The padding value to use for the concatenated inputs_ids.
   513→            device: The device for the concatenated inputs.
   514→
   515→        Returns:
   516→            A dictionary containing the concatenated inputs under the key 'concatenated_input_ids'.
   517→        """
   518→        concatenated_batch = {}
   519→
   520→        if is_encoder_decoder:
   521→            max_length = max(batch["chosen_labels"].shape[1], batch["rejected_labels"].shape[1])
   522→        else:
   523→            max_length = max(batch["chosen_input_ids"].shape[1], batch["rejected_input_ids"].shape[1])
   524→
   525→        for k in batch:
   526→            if k.startswith("chosen") and isinstance(batch[k], torch.Tensor):
   527→                if "labels" in k or is_encoder_decoder:
   528→                    pad_value = label_pad_token_id
   529→                elif k.endswith("_input_ids"):
   530→                    pad_value = padding_value
   531→                elif k.endswith("_attention_mask"):
   532→                    pad_value = 0
   533→                concatenated_key = k.replace("chosen", "concatenated")
   534→                concatenated_batch[concatenated_key] = pad_to_length(batch[k], max_length, pad_value=pad_value)
   535→        for k in batch:
   536→            if k.startswith("rejected") and isinstance(batch[k], torch.Tensor):
   537→                if "labels" in k or is_encoder_decoder:
   538→                    pad_value = label_pad_token_id
   539→                elif k.endswith("_input_ids"):
   540→                    pad_value = padding_value
   541→                elif k.endswith("_attention_mask"):
   542→                    pad_value = 0
   543→                concatenated_key = k.replace("rejected", "concatenated")
   544→                concatenated_batch[concatenated_key] = torch.cat(
   545→                    (
   546→                        concatenated_batch[concatenated_key],
   547→                        pad_to_length(batch[k], max_length, pad_value=pad_value),
   548→                    ),
   549→                    dim=0,
   550→                ).to(device=device)
   551→
   552→        if is_encoder_decoder:
   553→            concatenated_batch["concatenated_input_ids"] = batch["prompt_input_ids"].repeat(2, 1).to(device=device)
   554→            concatenated_batch["concatenated_attention_mask"] = (
   555→                batch["prompt_attention_mask"].repeat(2, 1).to(device=device)
   556→            )
   557→
   558→        return concatenated_batch

   560→    def simpo_loss(
   561→        self,
   562→        policy_chosen_logps: torch.FloatTensor,
   563→        policy_rejected_logps: torch.FloatTensor,
   564→    ) -> Tuple[torch.FloatTensor, torch.FloatTensor, torch.FloatTensor]:
   565→        """Compute the SimPO loss for a batch of policy model log probabilities.
   566→
   567→        Args:
   568→            policy_chosen_logps: Log probabilities of the policy model for the chosen responses. Shape: (batch_size,)
   569→            policy_rejected_logps: Log probabilities of the policy model for the rejected responses. Shape: (batch_size,)
   570→
   571→        Returns:
   572→            A tuple of three tensors: (losses, chosen_rewards, rejected_rewards).
   573→            The losses tensor contains the SimPO loss for each example in the batch.
   574→            The chosen_rewards and rejected_rewards tensors contain the rewards for the chosen and rejected responses, respectively.
   575→        """
   576→
   577→        return losses, chosen_rewards, rejected_rewards

   579→    def concatenated_forward(
   580→        self, model: nn.Module, batch: Dict[str, Union[List, torch.LongTensor]]
   581→    ) -> Tuple[torch.FloatTensor, torch.FloatTensor, torch.FloatTensor, torch.FloatTensor]:
   582→        """Run the given model on the given batch of inputs, concatenating the chosen and rejected inputs together.
   583→
   584→        We do this to avoid doing two forward passes, because it's faster for FSDP.
   585→        """
   586→        concatenated_batch = self.concatenated_inputs(
   587→            batch,
   588→            is_encoder_decoder=self.is_encoder_decoder,
   589→            label_pad_token_id=self.label_pad_token_id,
   590→            padding_value=self.padding_value,
   591→            device=self.accelerator.device,
   592→        )
   593→        len_chosen = batch["chosen_labels"].shape[0]
   594→
   595→        model_kwargs = (
   596→            {
   597→                "labels": concatenated_batch["concatenated_labels"],
   598→                "decoder_input_ids": concatenated_batch.pop("concatenated_decoder_input_ids", None),
   599→            }
   600→            if self.is_encoder_decoder
   601→            else {}
   602→        )
   603→
   604→        all_logits = model(
   605→            concatenated_batch["concatenated_input_ids"],
   606→            attention_mask=concatenated_batch["concatenated_attention_mask"],
   607→            use_cache=False,
   608→            **model_kwargs,
   609→        ).logits
   610→
   611→        all_logps = self.get_batch_logps(
   612→            all_logits,
   613→            concatenated_batch["concatenated_labels"],
   614→            average_log_prob=True,
   615→            is_encoder_decoder=self.is_encoder_decoder,
   616→            label_pad_token_id=self.label_pad_token_id,
   617→        )
   618→
   619→        chosen_logps = all_logps[:len_chosen]
   620→        rejected_logps = all_logps[len_chosen:]
   621→
   622→        chosen_logits = all_logits[:len_chosen]
   623→        rejected_logits = all_logits[len_chosen:]
   624→
   625→        chosen_labels = concatenated_batch["concatenated_labels"][:len_chosen]
   626→
   627→        return (chosen_logps, rejected_logps, chosen_logits, rejected_logits, chosen_labels)
   628→
   629→    @staticmethod
   630→    def get_batch_logps(
   631→        logits: torch.FloatTensor,
   632→        labels: torch.LongTensor,
   633→        average_log_prob: bool = True,
   634→        label_pad_token_id: int = -100,
   635→        is_encoder_decoder: bool = False,
   636→    ) -> torch.FloatTensor:
   637→        """Compute the log probabilities of the given labels under the given logits.
   638→
   639→        Args:
   640→            logits: Logits of the model (unnormalized). Shape: (batch_size, sequence_length, vocab_size)
   641→            labels: Labels for which to compute the log probabilities. Label tokens with a value of label_pad_token_id are ignored. Shape: (batch_size, sequence_length)
   642→            average_log_prob: If True, return the average log probability per (non-masked) token. Otherwise, return the sum of the log probabilities of the (non-masked) tokens.
   643→            label_pad_token_id: The label pad token id.
   644→            is_encoder_decoder: Whether the model is an encoder-decoder model.
   645→
   646→        Returns:
   647→            A tensor of shape (batch_size,) containing the average/sum log probabilities of the given labels under the given logits.
   648→        """
   649→        if logits.shape[:-1] != labels.shape:
   650→            raise ValueError("Logits (batch and sequence length dim) and labels must have the same shape.")
   651→
   652→        if not is_encoder_decoder:
   653→            labels = labels[:, 1:].clone()
   654→            logits = logits[:, :-1, :]
   655→        loss_mask = labels != label_pad_token_id
   656→
   657→        # dummy token; we'll ignore the losses on these tokens later
   658→        labels[labels == label_pad_token_id] = 0
   659→
   660→        per_token_logps = torch.gather(logits.log_softmax(-1), dim=2, index=labels.unsqueeze(2)).squeeze(2)
   661→
   662→        if average_log_prob:
   663→            return (per_token_logps * loss_mask).sum(-1) / loss_mask.sum(-1)
   664→        else:
   665→            return (per_token_logps * loss_mask).sum(-1)
   666→
   667→    def get_batch_loss_metrics(
   668→        self,
   669→        model,
   670→        batch: Dict[str, Union[List, torch.LongTensor]],
   671→        train_eval: Literal["train", "eval"] = "train",
   672→    ):
   673→        """Compute the SimPO loss and other metrics for the given batch of inputs for train or test."""
   674→        metrics = {}
   675→        prefix = "eval_" if train_eval == "eval" else ""
   676→
   677→        (
   678→            policy_chosen_logps,
   679→            policy_rejected_logps,
   680→            policy_chosen_logits,
   681→            policy_rejected_logits,
   682→            chosen_labels,
   683→        ) = self.concatenated_forward(model, batch)
   684→
   685→        losses, chosen_rewards, rejected_rewards = self.simpo_loss(
   686→            policy_chosen_logps,
   687→            policy_rejected_logps,
   688→        )
   689→
   690→        loss = losses.mean()
   691→
   692→        if self.sft_weight > 0.0:
   693→            if not self.is_encoder_decoder:
   694→                policy_chosen_logits = policy_chosen_logits[..., :-1, :].contiguous()
   695→                chosen_labels = chosen_labels[..., 1:].clone()
   696→            loss_func = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
   697→            sft_loss = loss_func(policy_chosen_logits.view(-1, policy_chosen_logits.shape[-1]), chosen_labels.view(-1))
   698→            loss = self.sft_weight * sft_loss + loss
   699→            metrics[f"{prefix}sft_loss"] = sft_loss.detach().cpu()
   700→        
   701→        reward_accuracies = (chosen_rewards > rejected_rewards).float()
   702→
   703→        metrics[f"{prefix}rewards/chosen"] = chosen_rewards.mean().cpu()
   704→        metrics[f"{prefix}rewards/rejected"] = rejected_rewards.mean().cpu()
   705→        metrics[f"{prefix}rewards/accuracies"] = reward_accuracies.mean().cpu()
   706→        metrics[f"{prefix}rewards/margins"] = (chosen_rewards - rejected_rewards).mean().cpu()
   707→        metrics[f"{prefix}logps/rejected"] = policy_rejected_logps.detach().mean().cpu()
   708→        metrics[f"{prefix}logps/chosen"] = policy_chosen_logps.detach().mean().cpu()
   709→        metrics[f"{prefix}logits/rejected"] = policy_rejected_logits.detach().mean().cpu()
   710→        metrics[f"{prefix}logits/chosen"] = policy_chosen_logits.detach().mean().cpu()
   711→
   712→        return loss, metrics
   713→
   714→    def compute_loss(
   715→        self,
   716→        model: Union[PreTrainedModel, nn.Module],
   717→        inputs: Dict[str, Union[torch.Tensor, Any]],
   718→        return_outputs=False,
   719→    ) -> Union[torch.Tensor, Tuple[torch.Tensor, Dict[str, torch.Tensor]]]:
   720→        if not self.use_dpo_data_collator:
   721→            warnings.warn(
   722→                "compute_loss is only implemented for DPODataCollatorWithPadding, and you passed a datacollator that is different than "
   723→                "DPODataCollatorWithPadding - you might see unexpected behavior. Alternatively, you can implement your own prediction_step method if you are using a custom data collator"
   724→            )
   725→
   726→        compute_loss_context_manager = torch.cuda.amp.autocast if self._peft_has_been_casted_to_bf16 else nullcontext
   727→
   728→        with compute_loss_context_manager():
   729→            loss, metrics = self.get_batch_loss_metrics(model, inputs, train_eval="train")
   730→
   731→        # force log the metrics
   732→        self.store_metrics(metrics, train_eval="train")

   734→        if return_outputs:
   735→            return (loss, metrics)
   736→        return loss

   738→    def get_batch_samples(self, model, batch: Dict[str, torch.LongTensor]) -> Tuple[str, str]:
   739→        """Generate samples from the model and reference model for the given batch of inputs."""
   740→
   741→        # If one uses `generate_during_eval` with peft + bf16, we need to explicitly call generate with
   742→        # the torch cuda amp context manager as some hidden states are silently casted to full precision.
   743→        generate_context_manager = nullcontext if not self._peft_has_been_casted_to_bf16 else torch.cuda.amp.autocast
   744→
   745→        with generate_context_manager():
   746→            policy_output = model.generate(
   747→                input_ids=batch["prompt_input_ids"],
   748→                attention_mask=batch["prompt_attention_mask"],
   749→                max_length=self.max_length,
   750→                do_sample=True,
   751→                pad_token_id=self.tokenizer.pad_token_id,
   752→            )
   753→
   754→        policy_output = pad_to_length(policy_output, self.max_length, self.tokenizer.pad_token_id)
   755→        policy_output_decoded = self.tokenizer.batch_decode(policy_output, skip_special_tokens=True)
   756→
   757→        return policy_output_decoded

   759→    def prediction_step(
   760→        self,
   761→        model: Union[PreTrainedModel, nn.Module],
   762→        inputs: Dict[str, Union[torch.Tensor, Any]],
   763→        prediction_loss_only: bool,
   764→        ignore_keys: Optional[List[str]] = None,
   765→    ):
   766→        if not self.use_dpo_data_collator:
   767→            warnings.warn(
   768→                "prediction_step is only implemented for DPODataCollatorWithPadding, and you passed a datacollator that is different than "
   769→                "DPODataCollatorWithPadding - you might see unexpected behavior. Alternatively, you can implement your own prediction_step method if you are using a custom data collator"
   770→            )
   771→        if ignore_keys is None:
   772→            if hasattr(model, "config"):
   773→                ignore_keys = getattr(model.config, "keys_to_ignore_at_inference", [])
   774→            else:
   775→                ignore_keys = []
   776→
   777→        prediction_context_manager = torch.cuda.amp.autocast if self._peft_has_been_casted_to_bf16 else nullcontext
   778→
   779→        with torch.no_grad(), prediction_context_manager():
   780→            loss, metrics = self.get_batch_loss_metrics(model, inputs, train_eval="eval")
   781→
   782→        # force log the metrics
   783→        self.store_metrics(metrics, train_eval="eval")
   784→
   785→        if prediction_loss_only:
   786→            return (loss.detach(), None, None)
   787→
   788→        # logits for the chosen and rejected samples from model
   789→        logits_dict = {
   790→            "eval_logits/chosen": metrics["eval_logits/chosen"],
   791→            "eval_logits/rejected": metrics["eval_logits/rejected"],
   792→        }
   793→        logits = tuple(v.unsqueeze(dim=0) for k, v in logits_dict.items() if k not in ignore_keys)
   794→        logits = torch.stack(logits).mean(axis=1).to(self.accelerator.device)
   795→        labels = torch.zeros(logits.shape[0], device=self.accelerator.device)
   796→
   797→        return (loss.detach(), logits, labels)

   799→    def store_metrics(self, metrics: Dict[str, float], train_eval: Literal["train", "eval"] = "train") -> None:
   800→        for key, value in metrics.items():
   801→            self._stored_metrics[train_eval][key].append(value)

   803→    def evaluation_loop(
   804→        self,
   805→        dataloader: DataLoader,
   806→        description: str,
   807→        prediction_loss_only: Optional[bool] = None,
   808→        ignore_keys: Optional[List[str]] = None,
   809→        metric_key_prefix: str = "eval",
   810→    ) -> EvalLoopOutput:
   811→        """
   812→        Overriding built-in evaluation loop to store metrics for each batch.
   813→        Prediction/evaluation loop, shared by `Trainer.evaluate()` and `Trainer.predict()`.
   814→
   815→        Works both with or without labels.
   816→        """
   817→
   818→        # Sample and save to game log if requested (for one batch to save time)
   819→        if self.generate_during_eval:
   820→            # Generate random indices within the range of the total number of samples
   821→            num_samples = len(dataloader.dataset)
   822→            random_indices = random.sample(range(num_samples), k=self.args.eval_batch_size)
   823→
   824→            # Use dataloader.dataset.select to get the random batch without iterating over the DataLoader
   825→            random_batch_dataset = dataloader.dataset.select(random_indices)
   826→            random_batch = self.data_collator(random_batch_dataset)
   827→            random_batch = self._prepare_inputs(random_batch)
   828→
   829→            policy_output_decoded = self.get_batch_samples(self.model, random_batch)
   830→
   831→            self.log(
   832→                {
   833→                    "game_log": wandb.Table(
